references.text: The daily burnt offering (tamid) mentioned here is the same as referred to in verse 31 and describes the basic requirements for the continuous offering.
The same phrasing 'in addition to the daily burnt offering' is used for the Sabbath offering, showing the pattern of additional offerings.
The same phrasing is used at the New Moon festival, where offerings come in addition to the daily burnt offering.
At the Passover feast, the requirement that the sacrifices must be without blemish (tamim) and come in addition to the daily burnt offering is repeated.
At the New Moon festival in the seventh month, the same pattern of additional offerings beyond the daily burnt offering is repeated.
During the Feast of Tabernacles, the phrasing about offerings in addition to the daily burnt offering, including grain and drink offerings, is repeated.
The original instruction regarding the daily burnt offering (tamid) that was to be offered morning and evening at the tabernacle.
The sacrificial regulations for the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot) in Leviticus, which supplement the instructions in Numbers 28.
The requirement that sacrificial animals must be without blemish (tamim) to be accepted by the Lord.
Ezekiel's vision of the daily burnt offering in the restored temple, confirming the continuity of the tamid offering.
